a13.speaker: Bola Tinubu, Nigerian President
a13.speech: Told the bloc's delegations to do "whatever it takes" to reach an "amicable resolution."

a13.speaker: One of the putschists (Niger junta, anonymous)
a13.speech: In a televised statement, warned Niger's junta would meet force with force in response to any aggression, with the exception of suspended friendly countries (an allusion to Burkina Faso and Mali).

a13.speaker: Niger junta (statement)
a13.speech: Blaming France's "careless attitude and its reaction to the situation," said it had "decided to scrap the cooperation agreements in the field of security and defence with this state" ; said "the functions of the extraordinary and plenipotentiary ambassadors of the Republic of Niger" to France, Nigeria, Togo and the United States "are terminated."

a13.speaker: Burkina Faso and Mali juntas
a13.speech: Warned that any military intervention in Niger would be tantamount to a "declaration of war" against them.

a13.speaker: Aissata Tall Sall, Senegal Foreign Minister
Mohamed Bazoum, ousted Niger President
a13.speech: Said that if the putsch proved successful, "it will have devastating consequences for our country, our region and the entire world." In a column in The Washington Post, called on "the US government and the entire international community to help us restore our constitutional order"; warned that Niger's neighbours had increasingly invited in "criminal Russian mercenaries such as the Wagner Group at the expense of their people's rights and dignity."

a13.speaker: Issiaka Hamadou, protester in Niamey
a13.speech: Said it was "only security that interests us," irrespective of whether it came from "Russia, China, Turkey, if they want to help us." "We just don't want the French, who have been looting us since 1960 - they've been there ever since and nothing has changed,"

a13.speaker: US State Department
a13.speech: Said the United States had chartered a plane to evacuate non-essential personnel and American citizens wishing to leave the country.

a13.speaker: France (government)
a13.speech: Said it had evacuated 1,079 people from the country, more than half of them French nationals.

a72.speaker: Binwell Mpundu, Nkana Independent Member of Parliament (Zambia)
a72.speech: Made a passionate appeal for unity following the US government's decision to halt all USAID-funded programmes for 85 days, and expressed deep concern about the impact on people living with HIV and AIDS and others dependent on US-sponsored projects. "The situation has become dire, especially for those living with HIV and AIDS." ; "Can you imagine how many of our brothers and sisters are employed through these projects?"

a115.speaker: Medical sources (Gaza)
a115.speech: Reported that the health sector in the Gaza Strip is experiencing a severe shortage of medical supplies and equipment for eye surgery, that 1,500 citizens have lost their sight as a result of the war of extermination while 4,000 others are at risk of losing it ; said that the eye hospital is on the verge of declaring that it will no longer be able to provide surgical services unless there is immediate and urgent intervention by the relevant authorities and international organisations.

a115.speaker: Unnamed female source at the Gaza City Eye Hospital (referred to only as “she”)
a115.speech: Added that the ongoing war of extermination has led to an almost total collapse of surgical services, especially for retinal diseases, diabetic retinopathy and internal bleeding ; pointed out that the Gaza City Eye Hospital currently has only three single-use surgical scissors, which are used repeatedly, increasing the risk to patients’ lives and preventing their survival ; explained that many eye injuries caused by explosions require medical supplies such as Healon and fine sutures, which are almost completely used up.

a212.speaker: Government of Zimbabwe
a212.speech: Has said the rehabilitation of the Cold Storage Commission (CSC), which was closed almost two decades ago due to viability challenges, will increase the daily slaughter of cattle from 60 to 2,000 per day.

a212.speaker: Monica Mutsvangwa, Information Minister of Zimbabwe
a212.speech: Addressing a post-Cabinet media briefing in Harare this week, said CSC was already negotiating...

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: On his main quality and main fault: said the question embarrasses him because it is difficult to judge oneself, and that “I forgive easily, but I forget with difficulty,” adding that others know his qualities and faults better than he does.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said the quality he prefers in others is honesty - “I like an honest person who makes his thinking clearly known” - which is even more important for a leader ; and that the fault he cannot bear is resentment, because “the resentful man is unpredictable” and “hatred, sourness, bitterness and resentment are more deadly than the venom of a cobra.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said the woman he admires most is Wangari Maathai, the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize, known as “the one who plants trees,” who created the Green Belt Movement ; and that he also admires the courage of his wife, Mpawenayo Gertrude, for her resilience during his long period in the bush, devoting herself to the education of their children.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Spoke with pride of his daughters' education - one with a Master's in Finance from Shanghai, one with a Master's in Computer Science from Bordeaux, and a jurist admitted as a lawyer by the Supreme Court of New South Wales in Australia.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said the man he admires most is Mwalimu Julius Kambarage Nyerere, who “had a vision for his country” and whose sobriety and pan-Africanism made him a respected and great political figure in Africa and the world.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said his happiest memory was the announcement that he had passed the inter-diocesan examination giving him access to the minor seminary of Kanyosha - “extraordinary news for me, for my parents and for the whole village.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said his saddest memory was the assassination of President Melchior Ndadaye on 21 October 1993: “We were beginning to taste the benefits of democracy and one morning... everything fell apart. We were going to live once again in fear and uncertainty about the next day.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said his greatest misfortune would be never returning to his native country: “I love my motherland dearly and I feel deeply unhappy without it.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Described 1 June 1993 as a historic date for Burundi, when for the first time a figure acceded to the supreme office through the ballot box and a Hutu was elevated to the presidency to the surprise of the former holders of power, with power shifting from Bururi to Muramvya province.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said he was in Bujumbura that day, where reactions were varied: in majority-Tutsi neighbourhoods disappointment was total and young university students demonstrated against what they called “an ethnic census,” while in working-class Hutu neighbourhoods such as Kamenge and Kinama Ndadaye's victory was welcomed with enthusiasm ; added that Ndadaye delivered a historic, unifying and reassuring speech, and yet some never stopped gnashing their teeth.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said the greatest feat in Burundi's history was the resistance to and victory over the slave trader Mohammed Ben Khalfan, known as Rumaliza, when King Mwezi Gisabo mobilised his troops to safeguard his people's dignity, adding that present and future generations should keep in mind that human life and dignity are priceless.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Named 1 July 1962 (independence) and 1 June 1993 (the victory of democracy) as the two unforgettable dates of Burundi's history.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said the most terrible dates for him were 13 October 1961, the assassination of Prince Rwagasore, which “left the people orphaned,” and 21 October 1993, the assassination of President Ndadaye, which plunged the country into a fratricidal war ; said that had they not been killed, Burundi's present trajectory would have been different.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Recounted as his worst war memory, besides the daily loss of comrades, being attacked by bees from a hive while withdrawing after a military operation, and being saved only by smearing his body with crushed cassava leaves.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said his memory retained no positive event from the bush - “Hunger, fatigue, the loss of friends, a permanent state of alert, that is life in the bush” - quoting Napoleon that “poverty, privation and misery are the school of the good soldier.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Corrected the premise that he returned to the country, saying the fighters never left national territory and only returned to Bujumbura ; recounted being reunited with his family on 31 December 2003 after seven years, returning “like heroes,” holding a press conference as FDD spokesman that astonished people who did not expect a bush fighter to speak French, Kirundi and Swahili so easily, and believing at the war's end in a pacified, reconciled Burundi committed to development.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Described his rapid rise within the CNDD-FDD: elected MP for Muramvya in 2005, appointed Head of State Protocol and then Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to Kenya, and recalled on 7 February 2007 to head the party.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said he was proudest, as Head of State Protocol and chairman of the celebrations committee, of having established punctuality and respect for timing at official ceremonies, which ended within five minutes of the scheduled time - “That was new.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said he was glad of the good rapport with the presidents of the chambers of parliament, Pie Ntavyohanyuma and Gervais Rufyikiri, and of having initiated permanent dialogue with the leaders of the other political parties in the National Assembly ; and glad to have avoided interfering in the Executive, describing his role as adviser rather than order-giver and addressing the Head of State directly to avoid two-headedness at the summit of the State.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said that if he had to do it again he would avoid no mistake: “I think I did what I could, as best I could, and I am proud of it.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Declined to say what decisions he would take as CNDD-FDD president, noting he was expelled from the party and that wisdom recommends speaking to those concerned directly rather than through the media.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said he took philosophically being blocked in Kampala when he tried to return for the May 2020 elections, calling it fair game in a period of electoral fever, but argued that after the elections there is no longer anything at stake and he should be allowed to return freely to his native country: “I keep hoping.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said that as president of Burundi his three urgent measures would be good governance (putting the right man in the right place, with a cult of excellence), effective implementation of the legal dividing line between technical and political posts, and a merciless fight against corruption and economic malpractice, quoting Shakespeare's “The Merchant of Venice” as a warning against corruption.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Defined democracy as a mode of government guaranteeing freedom of thought and opinion, free political and religious affiliation and participation through elected representatives, insisting it “is not reduced to the election period alone” but is a way of life and a culture, and that citizens must keep watch so the Republic does not become the property of a few individuals, quoting Maurizio Viroli: “Defective as it might be, a democratic republic is preferable to any other political system.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Defined independence as the right of peoples to self-determination and the capacity of leaders to decide freely and sovereignly, adding that a people is economically independent when citizens can meet basic needs without resorting to any assistance, that economic independence guarantees political independence, and quoting the English saying “who feeds you controls you” - concluding “We still have a big step to take before reaching true independence.”

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Gave as his motto “Be the best whatever you are,” an extract from a poem by Douglas Malloch.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Named his native commune of Bukeye and the view from Mount Saga as his favourite place in Burundi, recalling with emotion a childhood song about the country's beauty.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said his favourite song is Burundi's national anthem, which constitutes a political ideology and basic patriotic education ; that he listens attentively to “Yaramenje” by Nimbona alias Kidumu and “Umugabo w'ukuri” by Canjo Amissi, noting that such great men have often been lacking and Burundi has often sunk ; and that as a Catholic he listens with emotion to the “Adoro te devote” of Saint Thomas Aquinas.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said his favourite dish is wheat paste with a piece of well-cooked meat, without many ingredients, and that the journey he would like to make is to Mauritius, to learn the secret that makes it the most prosperous country in Africa.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said he is firmly convinced that man is born with a great potential to do good but also a propensity for harm, like a tree with two branches in which the best-watered branch grows best, quoting the Italian writer Fabrizio Caramagna that life is an invisible vase which overflows with anxiety or serenity according to what one pours in.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said death is an obligatory passage and the common denominator of the human species, quoting Francois de Malherbe on death's harshness, and that it is wise to think of it with serenity without making it an obsession.

a312.speaker: Jeremie Ngendakumana, former president of the CNDD-FDD party (Burundi), in interview
a312.speech: Said that before God he would give thanks for being kept alive in the most difficult moments, ask forgiveness for his failings, and ask Him to help the country find peace, stability and reconciliation.

a362.speaker: Adinya Arise Foundation (AAF)
a362.speech: Said the public hearing by the State Assembly marks a significant step towards ensuring the entrenchment of social justice and human rights in the state.

a362.speaker: Mabel Adinya Ade, Executive Director, Adinya Arise Foundation (AAF)
a362.speech: Describing the public hearing on the two Bills as "ground breaking", stated that the development promises to transform the lives of countless residents in Taraba state, and expressed her profound gratitude to State Governor Agbu Kefas and the State House of Assembly for their leadership and responsiveness to the issues at stake. "The passage of these bills represents not only a historic moment for Taraba but a commitment to restoring dignity, rights, and justice to those most affected by discrimination and trafficking." ; "Through our advocacy efforts, we strive to ensure that every citizen of Taraba is protected, empowered, and provided opportunities for a life free from exploitation and marginalization."

a362.speaker: Mabel Adinya Ade, Executive Director, Adinya Arise Foundation (AAF)
a362.speech: Observed that although the USAID project has officially come to a close, AAF has continued to push for the passage of the bills, underlining the unwavering commitment of AAF to the advocacy and protection of human rights; also expressed the hope that as the bills are on the verge of being passed, the leadership in Taraba state would continue to set the precedence for other states, reinforcing a commitment to human rights, equality, and justice for all.

a362.speaker: Speaker, Taraba State House of Assembly
a362.speech: Had recently announced the commitment of the state government to enact the Anti-Trafficking Bill at the just concluded Conference in Abuja on September 25, 2024, and reaffirmed the Assembly's support alongside that of the state governor; he explained that the collaborative resolve of the legislative and executive arms of government signals a shift in the government's desire to counter the activities of human trafficking and ensure the dignity, rights, and resources for persons with disabilities.

a396.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB) Group
a396.speech: Said US Secretary of State Antony Blinken's visit is historic and gives tremendous momentum to the institution's work to feed Africa, and highlighted the lasting impact of American investments in the Bank's operations, which align with Africa's shared priorities: "I commend Secretary of State Blinken's strong leadership and his commitment to food security, and I look forward to working closely with him and the US government to advance our joint efforts to help Africa feed itself and contribute to feeding the world," according to the African Development Bank's website; thanked the United States for its support to the Bank group's key agricultural initiatives and said he was delighted with the partnership between the two parties ; Also welcomed the new $9.5 million grant to support the Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation (TAAT) initiative led by his institution.

a396.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a396.speech: Praised the efforts deployed by the African Development Bank Group to help Africa feed itself and feed the rest of the world, on Tuesday 23 January in Cote d'Ivoire: "The African Development Bank is making the necessary investments in sustainable production in a smart and effective way, and, with its AfricaRice programme, it is maximising harvests and producing crops capable of withstanding climate change," satisfied with the positive and inspiring impact of the Bank's initiatives; he was as convinced as the US administration that there was enormous investment potential in climate-resilient and highly nutritious crop production, including certain neglected traditional African foods ; Expressed his admiration for the AfricaRice example.

a396.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina and Antony Blinken (joint commitment)
a396.speech: The two figures, who met at the headquarters of AfricaRice, committed to working together to identify partnership opportunities and to develop an investment strategy.

a398.speaker: Mahamud Moallim Abdulle, Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a398.speech: Announced that the country is facing a severe drought due to the delayed Deyr rainy season in September, October and November, and highlighted the need for focused efforts to support communities during this critical time ; Urged government agencies, affluent Somalis, and donors to come together in a unified effort to advocate for relief measures and to mitigate the impact of the drought; also expressed gratitude to governments and donors for their ongoing support.

a398.speaker: Recent reports (cited)
a398.speech: Show that over 5.98 million individuals need humanitarian assistance, with 3.2 million in critical situations; immediate action is required for nearly 200,000 people displaced by drought and to address the impact of famine, which has led to the loss of 1.4 million livestock.

a521.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a521.speech: Applauded the government of Eswatini for accommodating Mozambican nationals as refugees, providing them with necessary assistance ; commended the leadership of Eswatini for coming to the aid of Mozambicans and hopes the progress towards normalcy would lead to a safe return to their homeland ; "I would like to thank Eswatini as a country and within SADC that had taken on the responsibility to help our fellow citizens of Mozambique during the recent times; after elections, they went to courts, still they did not appreciate that thing. But the fact that you have to accommodate them, treat them well, and feed them on our behalf as SADC members, we have to thank you, and we are hoping that within this reasonable time, now that the thing seems to be calming down, they will be able to go back to their home."

a521.speaker: UN High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR)
a521.speech: According to the UN High Commission for Refugees, an estimated 1,500 Mozambican refugees sought asylum in neighbouring Eswatini after they fled post-election violence.

a603.speaker: United States government
a603.speech: Has denied accusations that it is funding people in order to participate in the mass demonstrations that have been taking place in Mozambique since 21 October; insists that the cash it hands out to families has nothing to do with Mondlane's demonstrations.

a603.speaker: US government (statement/note)
a603.speech: According to a statement, the US government claims that USAID and GiveDirectly are implementing a direct cash assistance project aimed at reducing poverty in disaster-prone rural farming communities: "The communities involved have been selected on the basis of need, in coordination with local authorities, civil society and the private sector. The project has no party or political affiliation. We strongly refute recent allegations on social media that falsely associate this project with partisan activities" ; "The organization addresses poverty in countries around the world by providing unconditional cash assistance to families in need. In 2021, USAID and GiveDirectly began co-financing programmes in Mozambique for cash assistance to communities in Sofala province that were devastated by the effects of Cyclone Idai" ; the note says that in 2024 the project expanded to Mogovolas district with the aim of providing capital to farming families to invest in improving agricultural production ; "This programme has demonstrated its ability to transform the lives of economically vulnerable Mozambican families, enabling them to prioritize investments for their own future."

a676.speaker: United Nations
a676.speech: Calls the drought affecting eastern and southern Ethiopia the worst drought the country has seen in four decades ; estimates some 13 million people are at risk of hunger in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia accounting for around a third.

a941.speaker: Regulators
a941.speech: estimate the gold can generate 59.4 million dollars in export revenues.

a1175.speaker: Government of Mozambique and Embassy of the United States in Maputo (joint public presentation)
a1175.speech: On Monday in Maputo they presented the 537 million dollar financing agreement under the second Compact of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), stating that the money is from the United States of America and will be used for the construction of climate-resilient infrastructure, coastal development and the strengthening of the local economies of Zambezia province that depend on agriculture and fisheries.

a1269.speaker: Liberian People's Party (LPP) (press release / party statement)
a1269.speech: Has spotted what it considers "redundant wastes" at the National Port Authority and is urging President Joseph N. Boakai to cease the expenditure of public funds that result from maintaining two separate boards of directors and two executive teams for the management of the Free Port of Liberia. The party says this redundant structure wastes resources and complicates the management of port operations. The LPP advocates for APM Terminals to continue its management of the Free Port of Monrovia, adhering strictly to the terms outlined in the 2011 concession agreements, and calls for APM Terminals to reimburse the Government of Liberia for all operational costs incurred on its behalf, including salaries of $13 million and $14 million that the NPA paid for 2023 and 2024 respectively. The party noted that the NPA, as landlord and regulatory authority, did not invest in purchasing or maintaining essential equipment or employing a significant workforce to manage daily operations at the port. The LPP also called on the Boakai administration to demand that APM Terminals publish comprehensive financial statements, urged APM Terminals to explain the recent increase in costs associated with NPA services and to undertake a comprehensive removal of debris and sedimentation, and stressed the importance of establishing a transparent and accountable process for the selection of inspection consultants, stating that the government exists to serve the interests of its citizens, not to exploit them through mismanagement or lack of accountability.

a1269.speaker: J. Yanqui Zaza, Chairman of the Liberian People's Party (quoted in a party release)
a1269.speech: Said that in this revised governance structure, the National Port Authority (NPA) would take on the role of both regulator and landlord, aligning with Landlord Port Governance principles, as the World Bank outlined in 2017. "What exactly is Landlord Port Governance? This model is characterized by a blend of public and private interests in port management. Specifically, the port authority assumes dual responsibilities: acting as both a regulator and a landlord. Meanwhile, operational activities, especially those related to cargo handling, are executed by private firms—in this instance, APM Terminals. This structure encourages collaboration and efficiency while allowing the private sector to leverage its expertise in port operations (as defined by the World Bank in 2007). How does the National Port Authority generate its revenue under this governance model? Consistent with Landlord Port Governance principles, the NPA generates income through various channels: first, it receives concession fees from APM Terminals; second, it collects maritime fees, which include rental income from piers and non-roofed accessories; and third, it earns rental income from storage facilities..."

a1269.speaker: World Bank (2007 and 2017 definitions of Landlord Port Governance)
a1269.speech: Outlined the Landlord Port Governance model, in which the port authority acts as both regulator and landlord while operational activities, especially cargo handling, are executed by private firms.

a1269.speaker: President Joseph N. Boakai of Liberia
a1269.speech: On August 5, 2024, reaffirmed a significant transition in the management of the Free Port of Monrovia, confirming the transfer of this vital asset from the state-owned National Port Authority to APM Terminals during a meeting with Mr. Igor van den Essen, Regional Managing Director of APM Terminals; Mr. Clay Crain, Managing Director of APM-Liberia; and Mr. Sekuu H. Dukuly, Managing Director of the NPA. The party quotes President Boakai as expressing a firm commitment to uphold the binding 2011 agreement, emphasizing the importance of safeguarding the interests of the Liberian people. He highlighted that this transfer is intended to bring about improved efficiency and operational effectiveness at the Free Port of Monrovia, ultimately benefiting the nation's economy.

a1271.speaker: Rural Self-Help Development Association
a1271.speech: said the termination of the aid jeopardised Lesotho's food security and economic prospects.

a1271.speaker: Estimates (unattributed trade figures)
a1271.speech: say the country imported more than 80 percent of its chickens and eggs.

a1454.speaker: Ministry of Justice of The Gambia (official statement)
a1454.speech: Issued an official statement concerning the conviction of Michael Sang Correa, qualifying the conviction as an "important milestone" and a "significant victory in the global quest for justice for victims of human rights abuses" ; "This conviction sends a clear message: the perpetrators of human rights violations will find no refuge," the statement says, recalling the Gambian government's commitment to "preserving the rule of law and guaranteeing justice for all victims of former president Jammeh."

a1454.speaker: Government of The Gambia
a1454.speech: Expressed its "deep gratitude" to the American government for "its unwavering commitment to justice," particularly praising the team of prosecutors who handled the case.

a1454.speaker: Ministry of Justice of The Gambia
a1454.speech: Announced that it is working to establish an Office of the Special Prosecutor to begin trials concerning the crimes investigated by the Truth, Reconciliation and Reparations Commission (TRRC).

a1454.speaker: US indictment (acte d'accusation) in the Correa case
a1454.speech: According to the indictment, the facts date back to the brutal repression carried out after the failed coup of 2006; alleged coup plotters were violently tortured at Mile 2 prison and at the headquarters of the National Intelligence Agency (NIA) in Banjul, by methods including beatings with military boots, pipes, electrical wires and sticks, as well as electrocutions, suffocation with plastic bags and even acid attacks.

a1454.speaker: Brian A. Benczkowski, US Department of Justice assistant attorney general
a1454.speech: When the case was opened, denounced Correa's "heinous acts of violence," aimed at extracting confessions through terror.

a1454.speaker: Pharing Sanyang, former commander at the presidential palace in Banjul in 2006 (witness)
a1454.speech: Testified that he still bears the scars of the abuse suffered after being accused of taking part in the attempted coup, and described Correa as "very aggressive" during the torture sessions aimed at extracting false confessions from him.

a1454.speaker: Ebou Jarjue, former waiter at the presidential palace in Banjul, 2001-2008 (witness)
a1454.speech: Testified that he was detained for more than nine months and then imprisoned at Mile II for four years, after being falsely accused of having tried to poison President Jammeh.

a1454.speaker: Tamsir Jasseh, former director general of immigration of The Gambia (witness)
a1454.speech: Testified that he was tortured and convicted on the basis of forced confessions for having helped a political opponent flee the country, despite his dual American nationality; he described Correa as "overzealous" and said that he "enjoyed himself" while torturing detainees.

a1495.speaker: Aliko Dangote, Africa's wealthiest businessman
a1495.speech: lambasted the continent's convoluted visa systems, criticising the need for 35 different visas which stifles intra-African trade. His critique was not only about red tape. It exposed more profound structural flaws that hinder Africa from tapping into its collective economic prowess.

a1495.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a1495.speech: touted these macroeconomic reforms as foundational steps toward sustainable growth.

a1495.speaker: Some diplomats in Addis Abeba (anonymous)
a1495.speech: quietly suggest it [Addis Abeba] is the only secure enclave left.

a1644.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a1644.speech: Declared mpox, a viral disease, a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 14 August 2024.

a1644.speaker: Ministry of Health of Uganda (reports)
a1644.speech: As of 18 December 2024, Ministry of Health reports show that 1,089 cumulative mpox cases had been confirmed in Uganda.

a1644.speaker: Anna Akola, 20-year-old mpox survivor from Meitu village, Pallisa District
a1644.speech: "I was feeling body pain, including in the joints. Sometimes I was feeling too much heat in my body. My eyes were red, and I could not eat because of the wounds in my mouth," recalls Anna.

a1644.speaker: Bernard Ikwaras, head of Pallisa District mpox disease surveillance
a1644.speech: Emphasized the need to avoid stigmatizing anyone with the disease and the survivors. "Anyone can catch mpox. It is therefore important that as a community, we support each other. When people recover from mpox, they can no longer spread the disease, so we do well to welcome them back into the community."

a1644.speaker: Charles Njuguna, Acting WHO Representative in Uganda
a1644.speech: "Based on Anna's experience, it is critical to scale up mpox awareness to the public and to ensure all health workers in both public and private health centres countrywide participate in webinars and capacity building sessions" ; "This will facilitate timely diagnosis and initiation of recommended treatment and other control interventions to stop the spread of mpox in the country."

a1751.speaker: International news agencies
a1751.speech: Are suggesting that the South African Minister of Foreign Affairs, Naledi Pandor, will push for military intervention.

a1751.speaker: Naledi Pandor, South African Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1751.speech: She said last September that she would go to the United Nations to request military intervention in order to prevent the spread of radicalism throughout the region.

a1751.speaker: Fernando Lima, journalist
a1751.speech: In his opinion, "there is still no clarity, and there are different forces and with different opinions on this issue" within Mozambique. There is a dilemma in the country. "I am sure that President Nyusi, as he did in his way of dealing with Afonso Dlhakama, will bypass the conservatives, and there will be a mix of interventions in Mozambique."

a1751.speaker: Fernando Lima, journalist
a1751.speech: Speaking to the private channel STV, argues that foreign aid must have support, so that it does not fall into the hands of the insurgents. "We will have to answer the question included in the plans of the South Africans who said: 'Very well, we will give military aid, but who will guarantee that it will not fall to the other side?' Military aid has to come, but it has to come with the elements to support it," he warns.

a1751.speaker: Lázaro Mabunda, journalist and commentator
a1751.speech: Says he has no doubt that it is not yet clear what kind of intervention is wanted in Mozambique. "I think this is the problem, because the Troika itself has floated ideas that there must be a military intervention. But I do not think that Mozambique is prepared or is clear about what type of intervention it needs at the moment. I think this is the biggest problem."

a1751.speaker: Lázaro Mabunda, journalist and commentator
a1751.speech: Suspects that there are different ideas on this issue within Frelimo, the ruling party. "There is a group that talks about the military issue, but there is another group that thinks that a military intervention does not make sense." ; "The president himself cites the example of Mozambique helping other countries, but he does not say how. But Mozambique also received help from some countries and, if we look at the type of support, it was mixed."

a1796.speaker: Critics (of the HPX deal)
a1796.speech: Argue that HPX's shift toward demanding access to existing infrastructure undermines efforts to establish an equitable railway policy that allows multiple users.

a1796.speaker: South Africa's Special Investigating Unit (SIU)
a1796.speech: According to the SIU, Gumede orchestrated an overpriced contract worth nearly R600 million (approximately $33.6 million) through Red Roses Africa, a company closely linked to him; the investigation found that Red Roses Africa dramatically inflated the price of essential goods—selling 25-litre containers of hand sanitizer to the South African Police at a 370% markup, generating nearly R400 million ($22.4 million) in excessive profits.

a1796.speaker: Robert Gumede, South African businessman and CEO of Guma Group
Mamaka Bility, Liberian Minister of State without Portfolio
a1796.speech: Announced the deal involving the importation of 285 units of earth-moving equipment for road maintenance in Liberia, which was allegedly conducted without proper procurement procedures.

a1796.speaker: Lawmakers and transparency advocates
a1796.speech: Have raised concerns about the lack of legislative oversight and the potential for backdoor dealings.

a1796.speaker: Senator Amara Konneh, Chair of the Liberian Senate's Public Accounts and Audit Committee
a1796.speech: Has called for a thorough review of the government's engagement with foreign investors; in a social media post, Konneh questioned why the administration would enter into informal agreements with politically connected businessmen without proper due diligence.

a1796.speaker: John Morlu, former Auditor General of Liberia
a1796.speech: Echoed these concerns, arguing that the government should acknowledge its missteps and subject such agreements to proper legislative scrutiny. "Government business cannot be conducted based on friendships and gentleman's agreements," Morlu said. "Transparency and accountability must be the guiding principles of Liberia's economic decisions."

a1796.speaker: Bronwyn Barnes, President and CEO of High Power Exploration (HPX)
a1796.speech: In an August 23, 2024, communication, proposed providing budgetary support for the formation of a National Rail Authority: "We are prepared to provide budgetary support to the Government of Liberia for the formation and initial operations of the National Rail Authority. This demonstrates our commitment to ensuring that the rail management system operates under the highest international industry standards and with full transparency."

a1796.speaker: Analysts and government insiders
a1796.speech: Believe this "budgetary support" is merely another form of financial inducement aimed at securing favorable terms for HPX; critics point out that this commitment comes as HPX seeks to finalize its Access Agreement with the government, raising suspicions that the offer is a strategic attempt to circumvent established procurement laws.

a1796.speaker: Guinean authorities
a1796.speech: Have reportedly stated that they will not permit their ore to be transported through Liberia.

a1909.speaker: Local fighters in Moqokori
a1909.speech: Described the delivery as an insult to those who have borne the brunt of the battle against Islamist militants.

a1909.speaker: Muse Salad, Hiran regional governor
a1909.speech: "This is not the first time. The people of Hiran have endured years of conflict, yet the government repeatedly sends aid that is neither adequate nor sincere."

a1909.speaker: Hawadle clan militias
a1909.speech: Reportedly viewed the meagre aid drop as a symbol of federal contempt.

a1909.speaker: Federal officials (no response)
a1909.speech: No federal official has publicly responded to the backlash or offered an apology to the affected communities.

a1909.speaker: Community leaders in Hiran
a1909.speech: Are demanding a transparent review of SODMA's operations and a commitment to equitable aid distribution.

a1942.speaker: Mamadou Moustapha Diarra, Chairman and Managing Director (PDG) of the Malian Company for Textile Development (CMDT)
a1942.speech: Welcomed the conclusion of this agreement, essential to ensuring both the cultivation and the marketing of cotton. He praised the availability and flexibility of the partner banks, in particular BDM-SA, in making available the resources indispensable to the campaign.

a1942.speaker: Ibrahima Ndiaye, Administrator/Managing Director (ADG) of the Development Bank of Mali (BDM-SA)
a1942.speech: Insisted on the crucial role played by the CMDT in the Malian economy as a key actor in the cotton sector. "Through this agreement, we reaffirm our commitment to supporting this strategic sector, a genuine engine of growth and development for thousands of farming families, as well as a pillar of the country's exports," he said. He declared that the campaign credit they have just put in place attests to the mutual trust and synergy between the CMDT and the banking pool. "It also illustrates our common desire to support agricultural production that is sustainable, competitive and generates value for the various stakeholders."

a1942.speaker: Ibrahima Ndiaye, Administrator/Managing Director (ADG) of the Development Bank of Mali (BDM-SA)
a1942.speech: Stressed the commitment and mobilisation of the member banks of the pool, which were able to unite their strengths and expertise to structure this financing. "The role of banks in such an arrangement goes beyond simple financing. It is tailor-made support, integrating the specificities and challenges of the sector, whether price volatility, climate issues or the imperatives of local processing," he maintained. According to him, this partnership will make it possible to consolidate the cotton sector as a lever of economic growth, encourage the financial inclusion of producers and cooperatives and support initiatives aimed at strengthening resilience in the face of environmental challenges. "Our collaboration with the CMDT and all the actors of the agricultural sector will continue to evolve to meet growing needs in terms of financing, innovation and modernisation of infrastructure," he promised.

a2044.speaker: Vera Songwe, Executive Secretary of the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a2044.speech: On whether countries will fully implement the AfCFTA agreement within the set timelines: "It's a good thing that some countries are moving a step ahead. It shows how trade is important to African countries and that countries are ready to open their borders. So yes, we are hopeful countries will fully implement the agreement. Countries are realizing they need to trade more with others because of an expected increase in revenues and jobs creation, especially for the youth. Intra-African trade is expected to rise to 53.3 %, meaning that revenues will increase."

a2044.speaker: Vera Songwe, Executive Secretary of the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a2044.speech: On how member states can ensure full implementation: "Ministers of finance of member states signing on to AfCFTA have an important role to play to help countries implement the agreement. Tax and customs, for example, which are key components of AfCFTA, are matters under the ministry of finance. It's up to the finance ministers to evaluate if, how and when revenues will increase for their countries and how these revenues will be expended. Once countries ratify the document, they have 10 years, some have 13 years, to put key policies in place to fully take advantage of AfCFTA. We expect countries to carry out a review of their macroeconomic policies, focusing on fiscal policies that are fit for purpose, and to help us not only to adapt to, and make the most of, AfCFTA, but more broadly to achieve Agenda 2063 and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The urgent action is to create the enabling fiscal space to foster both public and private investment while ensuring economic diversification."

a2044.speaker: Vera Songwe, Executive Secretary of the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a2044.speech: On contentious issues still to be agreed: "The remaining issues for discussion are matters regarding competition, provisions relating to investment, intellectual property, e-commerce and so on. Countries agreed to take more time to negotiate those issues. The issues are being discussed and will be finalized in the second phase of the negotiations. This is the same process even for other global trade agreements. Negotiations are never concluded at once; discussions on trade issues are broad and take time to be concluded. We want to avoid a situation where AfCFTA opens countries to unfair competition. Africa is leapfrogging in technology, which is why we are already discussing e-commerce. This is very important for countries that are well developed in technology. For those that are not so developed in technology, we must ensure they better understand matters around e-commerce."

a2044.speaker: Vera Songwe, Executive Secretary of the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a2044.speech: Advice to countries digitalizing their economies: "If fully embraced, digital applications will help fill credit gaps, empowering women to be entrepreneurs, providing real-time market data for rural and remote farmers as well as data analytics for climate-related information. The advantage of digitalization is that it transforms the economy by reducing barriers to entry and expanding market reach for businesses, creating jobs and boosting both domestic and foreign trade in goods and services. There is also an opportunity for African countries to capitalize on these developments to positively impact public service delivery, including the efficiency and reach of social safety nets, education and health outcomes. Already some countries are gradually embracing digital solutions for tax and expenditure policy, public financial management and public service delivery. Digital transactions could potentially reduce leakages in public spending and tax collection amounting to billions of dollars. That is money that can help fill a sizable gap in Africa's annual financing requirements."

a2044.speaker: Vera Songwe, Executive Secretary of the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a2044.speech: On her vision for ECA: "My idea is to see ECA provide ideas to transform the continent and create the conditions for economic growth and prosperity for the people. We want to be the think tank of Africa, through actions and results."

a2044.speaker: Vera Songwe, Executive Secretary of the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a2044.speech: On the strategy to achieve her vision: "My focus will be on transboundary regional issues like water sustainability, and political issues such as the dispute between the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic and Morocco. Globally, I will do more advocacy for Africa on taxation, migration, climate change, peace and security and trade. I am restructuring ECA by introducing specialized divisions on a range of issues. We now have the private sector, macroeconomic and finance, and poverty alleviation divisions."

a2044.speaker: Vera Songwe, Executive Secretary of the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a2044.speech: On her plan for women: "Despite various studies finding that women are central to the economic growth of any country or region, African women are still underrepresented in most sectors, including technology. Starting in-house, I plan to match the number of men staffers with equally qualified women. I intend to seek women's ideas in crafting policy recommendations. Our studies have established that too few women are involved in policy discussions and decision making. We are now working on the African Women Leadership Fund that will empower African women economically."

a2044.speaker: Vera Songwe, Executive Secretary of the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a2044.speech: On mobilizing resources for ECA: "We are looking to mobilize resources from traditional partners and build new partnerships with the private sector. Also, we will deepen our involvement with nongovernmental organizations. We hope to build bridges to the universities and other institutions for their valuable input, research and other matters."

a2194.speaker: Department of Climate Change & Meteorological Services (DCCMS), Malawi (update issued midday)
a2194.speech: Forecast that the chilly Chiperoni weather which most parts of Malawi experienced over a week ago is expected to return from tomorrow May 22; alerts the public that this is due to Mwera winds which are expected to start blowing on Lake Malawi and other lake water bodies from tomorrow with a speed of more than 50km/h, expected to cause high-water waves of more than 2m in height and to subside by Sunday, May 25 ; "During this period, we are also likely to experience Chiperoni Weather, which is associated with rain drizzle, windy, cloudy and chilly conditions — including fog patches over many areas beginning from the southern Malawi progressing northwards."

a2194.speaker: Department of Climate Change & Meteorological Services (DCCMS), Malawi (safety advisory)
a2194.speech: Offers safety advisories that people along lake water bodies should avoid fishing, swimming or using small boats and canoes during this period and to protect themselves from the chilly Chiperoni weather by wearing warm clothing, particularly the elderly and children; warns people not to use charcoal burners as a source of home heating inside closed windows and doors and that those with asthmatic conditions (mphumu) need to be extra cautious; advises motorists to exercise caution due to reduced visibility during foggy conditions.

a2194.speaker: MacDonald Gondwe, Disaster Risk Management Officer for Mzuzu City Council (MCC)
a2194.speech: Told MANA last week that they received disaster-related reports from Masasa, Chibanja, Chibavi and Mchengautuba East wards.

a2282.speaker: Central Office for the Prevention and Control of Drugs (GCPCD) (report)
a2282.speech: According to a report from the Central Office for the Prevention and Control of Drugs (GCPCD), the main drugs that the authorities confiscated are cannabis, heroin and cocaine. ; "The authorities seized in total 452.9 kilos of cannabis, valued at 1.35 million meticais; 79.5 kilos of heroin, valued at 47.7 million meticais; and 109.6 grams of cocaine, valued at 87,600 meticais", reads the report. ; According to the document, in the first six months of the year, the authorities also seized "416.8 kilos of methamphetamine, 4.2 kilos of hashish and 11.6 kilos of amphetamine, while no seizures of khat or morphine were recorded." ; According to the report, from January to June, a total of 214 criminal cases related to drug trafficking and consumption were instituted, of which 68 concerned trafficking of small quantities, 49 were for drug consumption, and 47 were for trafficking associated with other illicit activities. ; The report identifies three main routes used by traffickers: land (via the borders with Tanzania, Malawi, and Zimbabwe); sea, particularly through the ports of Beira, Nacala, and Maputo; and air, via Maputo and Nampula International Airports. It highlights that Mozambique continues to be a transit point for drug trafficking destined for South Africa and Europe. ; Compared to the same period in 2024, the report highlights a reduction, which "reflects an intensification of efforts to combat drug trafficking and consumption in the country", it claims.

a2468.speaker: Donald Trump, former US president (Truth Social post)
a2468.speech: Defended his record on NATO Monday, saying he had made it "strong": "I MADE NATO STRONG, and even the RINOS and Radical Left Democrats admit that" ; "When I told the 20 Countries that weren't paying their fair share that they had to PAY UP, and said without doing that you will not have US Military Protection, the money came rolling in. After so many years of the United States picking up the tab, it was a beautiful sight to see."

a2468.speaker: Donald Trump, former US president
a2468.speech: Speaking at a campaign rally in South Carolina on Saturday, Trump had described what he said was a conversation with a fellow head of state at an unspecified NATO meeting: "One of the presidents of a big country stood up and said, 'Well, sir, if we don't pay, and we're attacked by Russia, will you protect us?' I said, 'You didn't pay, you're delinquent? No, I would not protect you'" ; He said in a speech on Saturday that he would "encourage" Russia to attack members of NATO who had not met their financial obligations.

a2468.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a2468.speech: Slammed the comments as "appalling and dangerous", warning that his predecessor, who is running for re-election, intended to give Russian leader Vladimir Putin "a greenlight for more war and violence".

a2502.speaker: Head of the management committee of the Association for the Promotion of Tourism and Social Development of Daasbiyo (APTDSD)
a2502.speech: Recalled that they are driven and motivated to improve the living conditions of the inhabitants of Daasbiyo: "We always think of that famous quotation from President John Fitzgerald Kennedy, who said: 'Think about what you can do for your country and not about what your country can do for you.'"

a2502.speaker: Hawa Ismail, representative of the coordination of Civil Society Organisations with development aid partners within the regional council
a2502.speech: Made it known that thanks to this project, cluster 1 benefited from capacity building as well as from a USAID grant, and that the regional associations had the opportunity to have an equipped workspace following the equipment provided by the American cooperation agency at the headquarters of the regional council; she ended her remarks by deeply thanking USAID for its involvement on behalf of the well-being of the population, saying the project funding will significantly improve the quality of life of low-income households in Daasbiyo in terms of drinking-water storage.

a2502.speaker: Lauren Greubel, Deputy Representative of the USAID office in Djibouti
a2502.speech: Said she was happy to take part in this ceremony with the members of the association and the inhabitants of the village.

a2502.speaker: Omar Idriss Sougueh, Deputy Prefect (representative of the prefecture)
a2502.speech: Praised the efforts of the members of the Daasbiyo association for providing two 300-litre tanks to some sixty families, noting the handover comes at an opportune moment, the start of the hot season; he also thanked the USAID representative for their financial support and the members of the Kaizen company for their technical contributions to local civil society associations.

a2611.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA)
a2611.speech: Said Africa has fallen far behind schedule in its efforts to attain sustainable development targets (SDGs) by 2030; said in a statement on Tuesday that the continent is on track to achieve just 4 of the 169 measurable sustainable development targets by 2030, with 70 advancing too slowly, while 29 regressing.

a2611.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of UNECA
a2611.speech: Said Africa today finds itself navigating a complex web of poly-crises from climate shocks and mounting debt distress to geopolitical instability and the disruptive consequences of global financial fragmentation; these challenges are compounded by a decline in official development assistance and the erosion of long-standing multilateral frameworks, which together are creating a growing development vacuum affecting the continent.

a2611.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of UNECA
a2611.speech: Said Africa’s public debt surged to US$1.86 trillion in 2024, with the average debt-to-GDP ratio rising from 44.4% in 2015 to 66.7% today, and as a result resources are being diverted from other critical development priorities; said over 600 million Africans remain without electricity and 476 million live in poverty, including 149 million newly pushed into deprivation by climate and economic disruptions, and that these challenges demand urgent corrective action; added that the financing gap to achieve the SDGs in Africa has increased by up to US$1.3 trillion annually.

a2611.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of UNECA
a2611.speech: “While Africa’s GDP is set to increase to 3.8% in 2025 and 4.1% in 2026, this remains below the 7 percent growth needed to achieve SDG 8 and combat poverty, though it does exceed the OECD’s global GDP estimate of 3.1 percent.”

a2786.speaker: Sir Gavin Williamson, former UK defence secretary
a2786.speech: Told The Independent he has held talks with Trump's team about the official recognition of Somaliland, which holds a crucial strategic position on the Red Sea. “They should agree to it, though when he assumes office it will probably all take a little longer than we hope,” he said. “But had really good meetings with his policy leads so fingers crossed.” ; He added: “One of Trump's last orders as president was to withdraw troops from Somalia but then Biden countermanded that order. There is nothing that Trump hates more than someone overruling him so I used that to push the argument.”

a2786.speaker: US intelligence
a2786.speech: Flagged possible discussions with the Houthis – who are attacking shipping in the nearby Gulf of Aden – to provide weapons to the militant al-Shabaab in Somalia.

a2786.speaker: Sources in Washington DC (anonymous)
a2786.speech: Have told The Independent that the State Department “has warmed up” to the idea of supporting Somaliland's claim in the days following Mr Trump's victory.

a2786.speaker: Peter Pham, former US special envoy to the Sahel region and a senior official in the last Trump administration
a2786.speech: Noted: “I am sure this will be up for review after the inauguration. Similarly, a smooth election in Somaliland will, in addition to its other achievements, undoubtedly strengthen its case in an overall policy review.”

a2786.speaker: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office source (anonymous)
a2786.speech: Said: “It would be wrong to speculate on any policy decisions that the incoming administration of President-elect Trump may make. The UK, alongside others in the international community, does not recognise Somaliland's unilateral declaration of independence. It is for authorities in Mogadishu and Hargeisa to resolve Somaliland's status through dialogue and broad consultation.”

a2837.speaker: ECOWAS Conference of Heads of State (ordinary summit, Abuja, December 2024)
a2837.speech: decided to enact the exit of the AES countries, but mandated Diomaye Diakhar Faye, President of Senegal, and Faure Essozimna Gnassingbe Eyadema, President of Togo, for a final mediation for a period of 6 months to persuade the three AES presidents to give up their withdrawal plan and return to the sub-regional family; after that deadline ECOWAS will apply the measures required in the event of a member's withdrawal.

a2837.speaker: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger (joint withdrawal request to ECOWAS)
a2837.speech: decided to take their destiny in hand by addressing a request for withdrawal to the ECOWAS heads of state with immediate effect, on the pretext that the organisation has not worked better for the stabilisation of these countries.

a2837.speaker: President of Niger (General Abdourahamane Tiani)
a2837.speech: came out in the wake of the ECOWAS summit to reaffirm their common will to build an AES of the peoples that will take into account the deep aspirations of the peoples of the three countries that compose it.

a3042.speaker: Amir Ali, US District Judge
a3042.speech: Ruled in favour of the non-profit groups and companies that had gone to court against the funding freeze, which had forced them to cut services and lay off thousands of workers around the world; gave the Trump administration until Monday to pay the USAID money.

a3042.speaker: US Supreme Court
a3042.speech: Wednesday's ruling by the conservative-majority US Supreme Court reimposed a court order on the government to resume payments to international assistance organisations ; had instructed Ali to clarify what the government must do to comply with the earlier order, requiring the prompt release of funds to pay for work already performed ; referred the case back to a first-instance judge to set a new deadline, "taking into account the feasibility of any deadline for compliance" with its initial decision.

a3042.speaker: Samuel Alito, US Supreme Court Justice (writing for the four dissenting conservatives)
a3042.speech: declared himself "stunned" in his written justification of his vote. "Today, the Court makes an extremely unfortunate misstep by rewarding an act of judicial hubris and imposing a 2 billion dollar penalty on American taxpayers" ; "The court clearly expressed its frustration with the Government, and the plaintiffs raise serious concerns about payment for work performed" by international organisations, he acknowledged. "But the remedy ordered [by the first-instance judge] is an excessively extreme response."

a3042.speaker: Trump administration
a3042.speech: announced a week ago massive cuts to US international aid, including the elimination of 92% of USAID's funding for overseas programmes, boasting that it would "save taxpayers nearly 60 billion dollars."

a3257.speaker: Ministry of the Interior and Office of the UN Resident Coordinator in Djibouti (joint press release)
a3257.speech: Stated that the response is already under way and thanked all the partners who have contributed to the efforts, while noting that the response nevertheless calls for a surge of generosity from all our brothers and sisters around the world in order to respond as best and as quickly as possible to the needs of the victims.

a3257.speaker: Rapid humanitarian needs assessment (jointly launched by the ministries concerned, the UN System in Djibouti and NGOs under the leadership of the SEGRC)
a3257.speech: The assessment confirms that almost a quarter of the population has been affected by the floods and that 150,000 people require humanitarian assistance.

a3257.speaker: Moumin Ahmed Cheikh, Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a3257.speech: "I wish to renew our appeal to our partners, whom we thank immensely for the efforts already made to help us in this ordeal. We also thank you for giving more particular and sustained attention to supporting our government in its programmes of assistance to the affected populations."

a3257.speaker: UN Resident Coordinator in Djibouti
a3257.speech: Congratulated the government and all the partners for their good collaboration and stressed: "This humanitarian assessment is clear: there are urgent needs in Djibouti, we remain by your side and we call on the generosity of partners to increase and accelerate efforts in order to assist the most vulnerable, and to leave no one behind."

a3282.speaker: Senior official at the Reserve Bank of Malawi (anonymous)
a3282.speech: Confirmed what many already feared: “There is simply no forex left in the country. The situation is dire.”

a3282.speaker: Malawian student in China (unnamed)
a3282.speech: “We can’t receive money from our parents anymore. Cards from Malawi don’t work here. We are stranded, surviving on the mercy of friends.”

a3282.speaker: Malawian businessman in the United States (unnamed)
a3282.speech: “I went out for dinner in Indiana. When it was time to pay, my card failed. I had no cash. I left my phone at the restaurant as collateral until I could find a friend to help. It was the most embarrassing day of my life.”

a3282.speaker: Malawian patient in India (unnamed)
a3282.speech: “I came here for specialized treatment. I cannot use my card. Every transaction is declined. Imagine being sick in a foreign country and unable to pay for your own treatment. It’s terrifying.”

a3282.speaker: Malawian diplomat in Nairobi (unnamed)
a3282.speech: “We are representing the country, but we cannot even access funds for basic needs. How do we continue to serve when we can’t feed our families? This is a national embarrassment.”

a3282.speaker: Banks in Malawi
a3282.speech: Have quietly restricted international usage of local cards, citing “suspicious foreign transactions.”

a3282.speaker: Banking insiders (anonymous)
a3282.speech: Say the real reason is far simpler: there is no forex in Malawi to back up those payments.

a3316.speaker: Ministry of Health and the National AIDS and Health Promotion Agency (NAHPA) (joint statement)
a3316.speech: “This process is essential for policy decision making, ensuring efficient resource allocation, enhancing budget planning, progress towards National Strategy Framework for HIV and AIDS and advancing progress towards universal health coverage,” the ministry and NAHPA said in a joint statement on Monday.

a3373.speaker: Authorities (Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency)
a3373.speech: Confirmed that she will remain in custody pending further investigation and prosecuted in accordance with Liberian law.

a3373.speaker: Bill Cooper, Chief of Operations for the LDEA Nimba Detachment
a3373.speech: Reiterated the Agency’s commitment to eradicating illegal drug trade in the region and vowed to hold accountable anyone found in possession of harmful substances, citing the dangers such drugs pose to public health and societal well-being: “Drugs are illegal substances that negatively affect human lives and development. We will not tolerate their distribution or use.” ; called on individuals involved in the distribution, importation, or sale of illegal drugs to desist immediately, warning that violators will face the full weight of the law.

a3373.speaker: Residents/citizens of Nimba County
a3373.speech: Have commended the LDEA for its proactive efforts and increased vigilance in combating drug-related crimes, noting that under the current administration there has been a visible decline in drug activity across the county, in contrast to previous years when drug trafficking was on the rise.

a3427.speaker: Mory Kaba, Protection Officer at the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a3427.speech: Explained what is meant by an improvised explosive device: "According to the international mine action standards, an improvised explosive device is a device manufactured or deployed in an improvised manner, containing explosive materials or destructive, lethal, toxic, incendiary or pyrotechnic chemicals. It is designed to destroy, maim, distract or harass. Unlike conventional weapons, it acts without discrimination, striking combatants and civilians alike."

a3427.speaker: Mory Kaba, Protection Officer at the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a3427.speech: Said that although the use of explosive devices is not prohibited as such by international humanitarian law, their use is strictly governed by the fundamental principles of the conduct of hostilities - distinction, precaution and proportionality - and that affected areas must be located, marked and decontaminated, civilians must be informed of the risks, and "the placement or use of IEDs must under no circumstances cause excessive civilian harm or impede access to essential services."

a3427.speaker: Mory Kaba, Protection Officer at the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a3427.speech: Said improvised explosive devices act without discrimination: they kill, injure and maim, causing often irreversible physical and psychological after-effects, and seriously disrupt community life by preventing access to essential social services (schools, health centres, water points), compromising livelihoods (agriculture, livestock-rearing, markets), hindering the delivery of vital humanitarian aid, and slowing reconciliation processes in contexts weakened by conflict.

a3427.speaker: Mory Kaba, Protection Officer at the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a3427.speech: Said the ICRC carries out several activities for victims of explosive devices - emergency medical care, psychological care in ICRC-supported health facilities, physical rehabilitation in collaboration with the National and Regional Orthopaedic Fitting Centres, and economic assistance to help the most vulnerable victims regain their autonomy - and that, as part of prevention, the ICRC also conducts awareness-raising campaigns among the most exposed communities to reduce risks and strengthen resilience.

a3427.speaker: International mine action standards (cited norms)
a3427.speech: Cited as the source of the definition of an improvised explosive device as a device manufactured or deployed in an improvised manner, containing explosive materials or destructive, lethal, toxic, incendiary or pyrotechnic chemicals.

a3472.speaker: Brian Shukan, Ambassador of the United States to Benin
a3472.speech: “The results obtained are eloquent. Truly impressive results. Bravo!” — this declaration by Brian Shukan, Ambassador of the United States to Benin, at the closing ceremony of the “Farmer-to-Farmer” programme says much about the satisfaction resulting from the implementation of the programme.

a3472.speaker: Brian Shukan, Ambassador of the United States to Benin
a3472.speech: Said the programme is the manifestation of a successful collaboration between the government of Benin and the American government; recalled that agricultural development is a fundamental pillar of the government's Action Programme; observed, however, that access to modern technologies, to expertise and to resilient techniques was a challenge — a challenge that was met through the “Farmer-to-Farmer” programme.

a3472.speaker: Émilienne Cyuzuzo, interim resident representative of Catholic Relief Services (CRS)
a3472.speech: Observes that the “Farmer-to-Farmer” programme made it possible, among other things, to strengthen local capacities, to have innovative agricultural practices adopted, and to improve considerably the productivity and sustainability of farms; praised the commitment of all the actors involved in implementing the project ; “Through 'Farmer-to-Farmer', CRS is proud to have supported the ambitious programme of the Head of State, Patrice Talon, aimed at boosting agricultural competitiveness in Benin,” she noted ; said the success of this programme testifies to the powerful collaboration between the government and local and international partners in reaching shared objectives.

a3472.speaker: Émilienne Cyuzuzo, interim resident representative of Catholic Relief Services (CRS)
a3472.speech: Reports that in total 37 agricultural organisations benefited from the support of 101 technical assistance missions carried out by 87 American and local volunteers: “These missions made it possible to strengthen the capacities of more than 4,201 farmers, thereby benefiting a total of 17,644 participants. The net annual income of the organisations working in the cashew and soya value chains rose from 5.7 million dollars in 2018 to 7.8 million dollars in 2023” ; adds that more than 1.5 million dollars in resources were mobilised by the host organisations, with the creation of 27 new improved products in the soya and cashew value chains.

a3472.speaker: Abdoulaye Toko, chief of staff of the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries (MAEP) of Benin
a3472.speech: “I would like to express Benin's gratitude to the government of the United States which, through USAID, put in place this project, the fruit of a successful partnership between the Beninese government and the American government,” attested Abdoulaye Toko; he expressed the supervising ministry's satisfaction with the results obtained after five years of assistance to actors in the agricultural value chains, notably cashew, soya, oil palm and pineapple; and urged the American partner to continue its development actions alongside farmers.

a3675.speaker: Democrats from the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee (report)
a3675.speech: Said in a report released on Monday that China is increasing its diplomatic reach as President Donald Trump’s administration pares back America’s international presence; the 91-page report listed ways, from broadcasting to health programs and development efforts, that committee researchers said China is expanding its influence, and listed dozens of cases in which China had stepped in as the U.S. eliminated or cut back international programs, from funding vaccines and providing food to infrastructure development ; “China is pursuing a clear vision for the international order while the Trump Administration seeks to diminish America’s engagement globally,” the report said.

a3675.speaker: Critics (unnamed)
a3675.speech: Said the cuts would undermine Washington’s ability to defend and promote U.S. interests abroad.

a3675.speaker: Research published in The Lancet medical journal
a3675.speech: Said the cuts to USAID and its dismantling could result in more than 14 million additional deaths by 2030.

a3675.speaker: Trump administration / Trump officials
a3675.speech: Says its changes help align foreign policy with Trump’s “America First” agenda, and are part of a push to shrink the federal bureaucracy and cut what Trump officials say has been wasteful spending.

a3675.speaker: China (government)
a3675.speech: In May, after the U.S. terminated a $37 million HIV/AIDS grant in Zambia, China said it would help the African nation fight HIV/AIDS, including by donating 500,000 rapid HIV testing kits and planning more meetings to discuss its continued partnership on the issue.

a3832.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a3832.speech: Speaking at the slavery museum in Angola, addressed the future of Africa, saying that Africans will represent one in every four people by 2050 and that the destiny of the world is in their hands ; “The United States is fully committed to Africa,” Biden told Angolan President João Lourenço ; looking to the future, “I know that the future runs through Angola, through Africa,” said Biden, quoted by African News ; speaking on a stage near the water, he said that history cannot and must not be erased and that, although America was founded on the ideal of liberty and equality, “it is quite clear today that we have not lived up to that ideal.”

a3832.speaker: João Lourenço, Angolan President
a3832.speech: Called Biden’s visit a fundamental turning point in US-Angola relations, which date back to the Cold War.

a3832.speaker: African News
a3832.speech: Cited as the source quoting Biden’s remark that “I know that the future runs through Angola, through Africa.”

a3921.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a3921.speech: Recently during the swearing in of the new Minister of Finance and Planning, quoted as saying: “I am looking for a solution, this is why I bring somebody today and tomorrow I kick him out and bring another person. When I succeed in getting the right person, I will hold him firmly and will not let him go.”

a3921.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a3921.speech: In February this year during the swearing-in of the Chairperson of the National Bureau of Statistics, also quoted as saying: “We are trying to promote the young people that will make the real change that we are aspiring for.”

a3921.speaker: Eye Radio (editorial note)
a3921.speech: “The views expressed in this article are solely those of the writer. The accuracy of any claims made is the responsibility of the author and not of this website. The writer is a researcher and writer on local and international economic and political affairs.”

a3990.speaker: Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, Speaker of the House of Representatives (speaking through his representative, Hon. Patrick Umoh)
a3990.speech: Announced that the Federal Government is advancing plans for the Diaspora Voting Bill, which seeks to grant Nigerians living abroad the constitutional right to participate in national elections ; described the initiative as “a major step towards extending democratic participation to all citizens and ensuring that every Nigerian voice is heard in the process of nation-building” ; stated that the 10th House of Representatives regards diaspora engagement as a national priority, aligned with its legislative agenda of inclusion, accountability, and economic reforms.

a3990.speaker: Hon. Tochukwu Chinedu Okere, Chairman, House Committee on Diaspora
a3990.speech: Said that the NiSEDiG 2025 initiative was designed to create a unified policy framework combining institutions, legislation, and technology to improve Diaspora Governance ; explained that the newly launched Nigerians in Diaspora Response (NiDRes) App and Website would simplify how Nigerians abroad access government services and communicate with missions globally.

a3990.speaker: Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, Chairman/CEO, Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM)
a3990.speech: In her keynote speech, highlighted the remarkable progress made in diaspora engagements since the Commission's establishment six years ago: “Over the past six years, the Nigeria–Diaspora relationship has made groundbreaking strides in health, education, agriculture, ICT, transportation, and volunteerism” ; “We have now entered a new phase of consolidating diaspora engagement to boost national development” ; recalled that the National Diaspora Policy, approved by the Federal Executive Council (FEC) on April 28, 2021, provides the framework for facilitating diaspora participation in national development ; said the Diaspora Data Mapping Portal, launched in June 2021, continues to support data collection and informed decision-making ; noted that Diaspora remittances remain Nigeria's highest source of foreign exchange, amounting to US$23.81 billion in 2019 — approximately 6% of the nation's GDP ; listed several key initiatives spearheaded by NiDCOM, including National Diaspora Day, the Nigeria Diaspora Investment Summit, the National Town Hall Meeting, the National Diaspora Merit Award, and the Diaspora Quarterly Lecture Series.

a3990.speaker: Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, Chairman/CEO, NiDCOM (on challenges)
a3990.speech: Identified key challenges confronting NiDCOM, including limited funding, inadequate office accommodation, and the need to amend the NiDCOM Act to secure a sustainable funding mechanism from diaspora remittance charges.

a4003.speaker: World Bank (Malawi Economic Monitor, 21st edition, July 2025, ‘Navigating Uncertainty’)
